title: Validation evidence
description: What a validation phase actually ran, and what it reported. R22 requires validation to carry evidence, and the workflow event already carries an inline form of it; this contract is the standalone artifact for a validation whose evidence outlives the event — a layered validation whose checks come from more than one source. Each check names the command, the verdict, and the detail, so a reader can tell a check that passed from one that never ran. A check with no command is the case this exists to make impossible: an assertion that validation happened, with nothing that could be re-run to confirm it.

verdict.description: The closed set a consumer branches on. a failure back to implementation under the workflow's stated attempt limit.

checks.description: Every check that ran. Empty would be a verdict with nothing behind it.

check.description: The command, so the check can be re-run rather than believed.

detail.description: What it reported. On `not-run`, why it did not — a missing check is named as not run rather than reported as satisfied.

then.description: A passing verdict over a failing check is a false report. A `not-run` check is permitted and visible, which is the honest form of partial coverage.
